newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian annual inflation rises to 26.7 pct in January.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian annual inflation rises to 26.7 pct in January.

text.p: Annual inflation in Nigeria rose to 26.7 percent in January 1997 from 25.6 percent in December, the government statistics office said on Wednesday.
The rise was caused by higher food prices, offset by lower prices for clothing, footwear and household appliances.
Nigeria's military government has set an inflation target of 15 percent for 1997 compared with an average 28 percent recorded in 1996.
But analysts fear that while the overall inflation trend is falling a big leap in money supply aimed at promoting economic growth could cause it to rise again.
The Petroleum Trust Fund, set up to disburse money accruing from a big rise in pump prices in 1994, has lodged billions of naira in commercial banks for roads and other public projects.
But an official decision to move accounts of government companies to commercial banks from the central bank is being delayed in order not to pump too much money into circulation.
